schedule: before 9am on the first day of the month

packageRules.description: Inference engine pins (ollama/uv/vllm/hf_transfer) — own PR each (each needs its own validation), labelled inference, stable-only

An ollama bump needs no checksum recomputed (the installer verifies against the release's own sha256sum.txt) but DOES need that file, and the asset names, to still be there — this note tells the reviewer what to run
prBodyNotes: :mag: **ollama version bump**: no hash to update here — unlike uv, the installer fetches the release's own `sha256sum.txt` and verifies every archive against it (see `OllamaPinnedVersion`'s doc). What that assumes, and what this bump has to confirm, is that the new release still publishes that file and still names its assets the same way — `0.30.x` renamed the Linux archive from `.tgz` to `.tar.zst`, which 404s exactly one OS. Run `make integration-runtime` (or `go test -tags integration -run TestPinnedReleasePublishesEveryAssetChecksum ./internal/runtime/`) on this branch: it checks all four (goos, goarch) pairs we ship against the real release.

packageRules.description: A vllm bump now rebuilds the venv on every installed host (#843), and the product emits parser names and serve flags read out of the pinned release, so the bump has to confirm they still exist
prBodyNotes: :warning: **vllm version bump**: this is no longer only what a FRESH install gets. Since #843 every host with a venv rebuilds it on its next update (~6 GB, ~5-15 min), so a bump reaches the whole fleet. Two things to confirm against the new release before merge, because vLLM turns either into a dead engine rather than a degraded one: (1) every `--tool-call-parser` name in `cmd/waired-agent/inference_vllm_toolparser.go` is still registered (`_TOOL_PARSERS_TO_REGISTER` in `vllm/tool_parsers/__init__.py`) — an unregistered name is rejected at start-up; (2) every flag `runtime.VLLMAdapter.commandArgs` emits still exists (`vllm/engine/arg_utils.py`, `entrypoints/openai/cli_args.py`) — an unknown flag is an argparse exit 2 and all of EnsureRunning's retries fail. `TransformersConstraint` and `VLLMVerifyImports` are pinned to this release too; bump them in the same PR after verifying on a real GPU host.

packageRules.description: uv bump also needs UVPinnedSHA256Linux64 recomputed; postUpgradeTasks does it when self-hosted Renovate is allowed to run commands, else this note + label tell the reviewer
prBodyNotes: :warning: **uv version bump**: `UVPinnedSHA256Linux64` in `internal/runtime/uv.go` must match the new tarball. `scripts/dev/update-uv-sha.sh` recomputes it via postUpgradeTasks when self-hosted Renovate has `allowedPostUpgradeCommands` enabled; otherwise run it by hand on this branch before merge.
